findings.source: arXiv:2512.03989 (Teaching Old Tokenizers New Words), HTML v1
findings.numbers: ≤9.6% bytes/token gain vs naive extension; win rate 72.9–100% over 70 langs; 1K–32K added tokens; 26% CPT-time reduction
findings.relevance: Drop-in upgrade for the tokenizer work package: if the panel picks expansion (not swap), extend Qwen3's tokenizer via continued BPE on the 9–10B-token Kazakh corpus, not Sherkala's merge-append. Whether Kazakh is among the 70 languages is unconfirmed.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] ZeTT (Zero-Shot Tokenizer Transfer): a hypernetwork predicts embeddings for an ARBITRARY new tokenizer; on Mistral-7B and XLM-R the swapped model stays close to original performance and 'the remaining gap can be quickly closed by continued training on less than 1B tokens'. Hypernetworks trained on base models transfer to fine-tuned variants. Complementary cheap path: NorMistral's 3-stage swap (KB) needed only 1,000 frozen-body embedding-only steps before full CPT.
findings.source: arXiv:2405.07883 (ZeTT, Minixhofer et al.); NorMistral arXiv:2412.06484 (KB, not re-verified)
findings.numbers: <1B tokens to close swap gap at 7B; hypernetwork training cost not budgeted here
findings.relevance: Makes full tokenizer replacement (needed for fertility <2.0; expansion only reached 2.04 at Sherkala) a bounded-cost option inside a ~10B-token budget; untested at 0.6B and on Kazakh Cyrillic.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested, single-GPU regime] LLiMba (2026): Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct adapted to Sardinian on ONE 24GB consumer GPU with only 11.5M target-language tokens + 2.4M related-Romance tokens (CPT → ppl 6.76), then SFT comparison: rsLoRA r=256 reached 28.5 BLEU (En→Sardinian) vs full fine-tuning 21.0 and CPT-only 17.3; conclusion 'adapter capacity matters more than the choice among LoRA variants'. Note this is the extreme-low-data regime where full FT overfits — opposite conclusion to the 20B-token CPT regime of arXiv:2405.09673.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.09015 (LLiMba)
findings.numbers: 11.5M+2.4M tokens; 24GB GPU; rsLoRA-r256 28.5 BLEU vs full-FT 21.0 vs CPT 17.3; CPT ppl 6.76
findings.relevance: Maps the LoRA-vs-full crossover: with ≥1B tokens (lab's case) full CPT wins; below ~100M tokens high-rank LoRA wins. Also proof that meaningful adaptation runs fit consumer/Kaggle GPUs.

findings.claim: [tested-on-Russian, kk/ru-adjacent] Learned Embedding Propagation (LEP, Tikhomirov & Chernyshev 2024): after vocab adaptation + limited CPT of the BASE model (deliberately limiting which parameters move), the learned embeddings are propagated/implanted directly into any existing INSTRUCT-tuned variant, skipping instruction tuning entirely. Tested on LLaMa-3-8B and Mistral-7B across 4 Russian tokenization variants; regains and sometimes exceeds the original instruct model's quality (Darumeru benchmark; competitive with OpenChat-3.5 and Llama-3-8B-Instruct); further gains from self-calibration + light continued instruct-tuning.
findings.source: arXiv:2412.21140 (LEP) — method and results read from PDF text; exact per-benchmark numbers not extracted
findings.numbers: 2 backbones × 4 tokenization variants; benchmark = Darumeru (Russian); exact deltas in Fig.1/paper tables
findings.relevance: Cheap route to a QymyzLM-Chat: do vocab+CPT once on Qwen3-0.6B-Base, then implant embeddings into Qwen3-0.6B (instruct) instead of building a Kazakh SFT corpus — untested on Kazakh and at 0.6B.

findings.claim: [tested-on-Kazakh] ISSAI KazLLM-1.0-8B (Dec 2024): Llama-3.1-8B customized primarily via instruction-tuning per its HF card ('customized by ISSAI to improve helpfulness'); NO tokenizer change (Kazakh fertility stays ~4.73); license CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial). Press claims a 150B-token multilingual corpus (kk/ru/en/tr) but the card does not document CPT token counts. Independent measurement (Sherkala paper): KazMMLU 37.0 vs Sherkala-8B chat 41.4. Card's own leaderboard: kk avg 56.85, en avg 76.4, ru avg 61.4 (custom task suite, not KazMMLU).
findings.source: huggingface.co/issai/LLama-3.1-KazLLM-1.0-8B (card fetched); issai.nu.edu.kz/kazllm; KazMMLU 37.0 from arXiv:2503.01493 (KB)
findings.numbers: 8B params; KazMMLU 37.0; CC BY-NC 4.0; 150B-token corpus claim [card-unconfirmed]
findings.relevance: The national-flagship 8B without tokenizer surgery scores 4.4pp below Sherkala WITH tokenizer surgery — evidence that fertility/tokenizer work, not just data volume, drives Kazakh exam gains. Its NC license also leaves the open-license niche empty for QymyzLM.

findings.claim: [tested-on-Kazakh] Irbis-7b (Gen2B, 2024): community Kazakh adaptation; the Instruct variant is a LoRA fine-tune of their own Irbis-7b-v0.1 base on 200K Kazakh (question, context, answer) examples; MIT license; NO published benchmarks (card admits it only 'handles simple questions well'); LoRA rank undisclosed. AlemLLM (astanahub, 2025): 247B-total/22B-active MoE, 56 layers, vocab 100,352, SentencePiece, kk/ru/en/tr; training token count undisclosed.
findings.source: huggingface.co/Gen2B/Irbis-7b-Instruct_lora (card fetched); huggingface.co/astanahub/alemllm via search + skywork summary
findings.numbers: Irbis: 200K SFT pairs, MIT, 0 benchmarks; AlemLLM: 247B/22B MoE, vocab 100,352
findings.relevance: Kazakh CPT landscape check: no ≤1.5B open Kazakh CPT model with published recipe+numbers exists (SozKZ is from-scratch) — QymyzLM's niche is uncontested; benchmark-less community LoRA efforts are the cautionary baseline.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] LR-schedule evidence CONFLICTS across the three strongest CPT recipes — do not average: (a) Ibrahim 2403.08763: re-warm to high LR then re-decay (+replay) matches union re-training at 405M; (b) NVIDIA 'Reuse, Don't Retrain' (15B, 8T-token base): start at η_min of pretraining (4.5e-5), cosine to η_min/100, NO warmup, switch general→QA blend at η_max/5, giving +9% relative avg accuracy at 300B CPT tokens (48.9%→55.4% cumulative +13%); (c) Sailor 0.5B: constant 1e-4 (recovery-friendly); (d) EstLLM: trapezoidal WSD. NVIDIA explicitly warns re-warming a heavily-trained base can hurt; Ibrahim shows not re-warming slows adaptation.
findings.source: arXiv:2407.07263 (Reuse Don't Retrain) HTML v1; arXiv:2403.08763 PDF; arXiv:2404.03608; arXiv:2603.02041
findings.numbers: NVIDIA: η_min 4.5e-5 → 4.5e-7, no warmup, +9%@300B; Ibrahim: rewarm+redecay+5–25% replay; Sailor: 1e-4 constant
findings.relevance: Qwen3-0.6B is a heavily-overtrained base (KB: transfer benefit decays log with base tokens) — the panel must pick a schedule; WSD/constant-with-final-decay is the only family compatible with interruptible Kaggle sessions AND both papers' cautions.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] Token-budget envelope for measurable gains when adapting ≤1.5B-class models: ~2B tokens suffice for vocab-expansion integration (EEVE, 2.8–10.8B); <1B closes a full tokenizer-swap gap at 7B (ZeTT); ~1.2B tokens/language taught Galician/Swahili/Urdu to 7–8B bases (LayRA, KB); but 140B SEA tokens at 0.5B moved QA strongly and exams not at all (Sailor); and 20B code tokens at 7B raised HumanEval by +14.4pp absolute over base (LoRA-learns-less full-FT). No published study isolates 'minimum Kazakh tokens for KazMMLU movement at 0.6B' — the lab's ~10B-token corpus with ≤4-epoch repetition (KB: 2305.16264) supports an effective budget of ~20–40B tokens-seen.
findings.numbers: 2B (vocab integration) / <1B (swap realign) / 1.2B per language (LayRA) / 140B→0 exam pts at 0.5B; 9–10B kk corpus ×4 epochs ≈ 36–40B tokens-seen ceiling
findings.relevance: Feasibility anchor for the compute plan: the tokenizer/embedding work fits in the first 1–2B tokens; the KazMMLU-moving phase must be data-quality-driven (instruction-augmented + synthetic textbook MT à la Sherkala's 24%) inside a ≤40B tokens-seen budget.

findings.claim: [tested-on-Kazakh] KazByte (arXiv:2603.27859) status re-check 2026-07: still a methods/position paper — Stage B trains only attention weights (W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O + input LayerNorm) of Qwen2.5-7B with a frozen byte-level adapter, on the SozKZ 9B-token corpus (saken-tukenov/sozkz-corpus-clean-v3, 48.2% pass rate from 28.4M raw docs); evaluation is still a PLAN (MCQA/Belebele/SIB-200 vs Qwen2.5-7B+BPE and SozKZ-600M), no reported numbers found. Consistent with KB — no contradiction.
findings.source: arXiv:2603.27859 HTML via search snapshot (2026-07-04)
findings.numbers: SozKZ corpus 9B tok, 18 sources, 9-stage cleaning, 48.2% pass; results: none published
findings.relevance: Confirms the Kazakh sub-1B CPT-with-numbers slot remains open; also flags the attention-only CPT variant (freeze FFN) as a Kazakh-proposed but still unvalidated recipe the panel could pilot cheaply.

recommendations: Default training mode: switch the spec from QLoRA-CPT to FULL-parameter fp16 CPT of Qwen3-0.6B. Evidence: BLOOM+1 (full CPT best at 560M, adapters win only >3B) + LoRA-learns-less (LoRA r=256 ≈ full FT at 1/5 the tokens, −9pp GSM8K at equal budget). Memory check to re-derive in the spec: 596M params → fp16 weights 1.19GB + fp32 AdamW m/v 4.77GB + fp32 master 2.38GB + grads ≈ 9.5GB states, feasible on T4x2 (2×15GB) with ZeRO-2 or 8-bit Adam; keep QLoRA (rank ≥256, all linear layers, rsLoRA scaling) only as the fallback if activation memory at 4K ctx doesn't fit.

CPT mixture (drop-in): Kazakh 65–75%, replay 25–35% split ru+en, with code/math/instruction-augmented components inside the replay share (EstLLM pattern; Ibrahim 25% strong-shift floor; Sailor 30%; DeepSeek-V2 30%). Prioritize curated Kazakh sources over raw MADLAD/mC4/FineWeb-2 slices — EstLLM showed curated national corpora beat larger MT-spam-polluted web dumps, and Kazakh web is at least as MT-polluted.

LR schedule: WSD/trapezoidal (warmup → constant ~1e-4-scale → decay on demand), NOT cosine — the only family endorsed by Sailor (interruption recovery, matches Kaggle session bursts) and EstLLM, and it sidesteps the unresolved rewarm-vs-no-rewarm conflict (Ibrahim 2403.08763 vs NVIDIA 2407.07263) by re-warming once and never restarting. Report both cited positions in the spec; do not average.

Tokenizer: present BOTH options to the panel with the param math attached. (A) Expansion: +8–10K Kazakh tokens via continued-BPE training (arXiv:2512.03989, NOT Sherkala's merge-append), subword-mean init (fancy init washes out after ~0.5B tokens, arXiv:2407.05841), EEVE-style staged unfreeze adapted to TIED embeddings; cost +8–10M params, fertility improvement partial. (B) Full swap to a ~60K Kazakh-centric vocab (SozKZ-style) via ZeTT/FVT init + NorMistral 1000-step frozen-body realign; hits fertility <2.0 AND frees ~94M params of the 600M budget for Engram tables. Option B is the only one that satisfies both the fertility target and the param cap simultaneously.

Do NOT untie Qwen3-0.6B's embeddings (costs +155.6M params, instantly breaking the budget); any vocab-expansion staging must be a tied-weights variant — flag in the spec that this exact configuration (staged vocab expansion on tied embeddings at 0.6B) is untested anywhere and is itself a publishable micro-ablation.

KazMMLU strategy: budget the exam-score gains to knowledge-dense data, not token volume — Sailor's 140B tokens moved exams 0.0pp at 0.5B. Concretely: instruction-augmented CPT (Instruction Pre-Training, per EstLLM), Sherkala's synthetic-textbook-MT trick (24% of their Kazakh corpus), and the Engram memory axis; treat raw-web CPT as fluency/retrieval fuel only.
Chat variant: pilot LEP (arXiv:2412.21140) — implant post-CPT embeddings into Qwen3-0.6B instruct instead of building a Kazakh SFT corpus; cheap, and a first-ever-at-0.6B/on-Kazakh datapoint.

Run one in-house pilot before the panel locks the recipe: 100–200M-token 3-arm comparison (full CPT vs QLoRA-r256 vs attention-only-CPT à la KazByte) on identical data with KazMMLU-dev + held-out kk perplexity — no published head-to-head exists at 0.6B, and this table is itself paper material.
open_questions: QLoRA specifically (4-bit NF4 base + LoRA) vs bf16-LoRA vs full CPT has NO published quality head-to-head in the CPT regime at any scale — all cited evidence is 16-bit LoRA; the 4-bit base quantization error during 10B-token CPT on a 0.6B model is unmeasured.

Does fp16 (no bf16 on T4) full CPT of a bf16-native Qwen3 checkpoint stay loss-stable at LR ~1e-4, or does it need fp32 master weights + aggressive loss scaling? No published fp16-T4 CPT report found for Qwen3.
Minimum Kazakh token count for statistically significant KazMMLU movement at 0.6B — unpublished; the pilot recommendation addresses this.
Is Kazakh among the 70 languages in arXiv:2512.03989's continued-BPE evaluation? (Estonian confirmed; Kazakh unconfirmed — check their appendix at ingest.)
ISSAI KazLLM's press-claimed 150B-token CPT corpus vs the HF card's instruction-tuning-only description — unresolved; affects whether 37.0 KazMMLU counts as a CPT or SFT datapoint.
LEP's exact Darumeru deltas and whether embedding propagation survives a tokenizer SWAP (not just expansion) — paper tables not fully extracted; re-read before citing numbers.

Sherkala reports KazMMLU base 51.6 vs chat 41.4 (KB) — if instruct-tuning costs −10pp there, does the lab's 32.8% Qwen3-0.6B-Base target imply comparing base-to-base only? Protocol decision needed before any published claim.

findings.claim: SozKZ built the largest known monolingual Kazakh pretraining corpus by aggregating 18 web/curated sources (CulturaX, HPLT 2.0, mC4, MADLAD-400, mOSCAR, CC-100, Kazakh Wikipedia, kz-transformers/multidomain-kazakh-dataset). Raw = 28.4M docs; a 9-stage RULE-BASED cleaning pipeline (NFC, control-char removal, whitespace collapse, min-length >=50 chars, URL density <=5/1000 chars, HTML tags <=5, Kazakh char-ratio filter, langID kk-only, MD5 EXACT dedup within+cross-source vs 12.4M multidomain hashes) kept 13.7M docs (48.2% pass rate) = ~9.0B tokens under a 50K BPE tokenizer. Trained 1 epoch only, tokens/param 15.3:1 for the 600M.
findings.numbers: 18 sources; 28.4M raw docs -> 13.7M kept (48.2%) -> ~9.0B tokens (50K BPE); MD5 exact dedup only; 1 epoch; 9.0B/587M = 15.3:1
findings.relevance: This is the concrete from-scratch Kazakh data ceiling and pipeline the lab can reuse. Two exploitable gaps: (a) only MD5 EXACT dedup (no MinHash fuzzy dedup) and (b) NO model-based quality filter and (c) only 1 epoch — all three are where 2026 English/German recipes add the most value.

findings.claim: SozKZ-600M (from-scratch, ~9.0B kk tokens, dedicated 50K Kazakh BPE) scores BELOW our Qwen3-0.6B target on knowledge: MC QA (kk-socio-cultural, 7,111 Q, 4-choice, 0-shot logit-scored) 30.3% vs Qwen-0.5B 31.5%, Llama-3.2-1B 32.0%, Qwen-1.5B 37.1%; Belebele-kk 27.0% (near 25% floor for all sub-3B); SIB-200-kk 25.5% (beats all multilingual up to 2B incl Qwen-1.5B 11.8%, Gemma-2B 20.1% — tokenizer/lexical win). MC QA scaled 22.8%(50M)->30.3%(600M), no saturation.
findings.source: arXiv:2603.20854 (SozKZ), Table 2
findings.numbers: SozKZ-600M: MC QA 30.3 / Belebele 27.0 / SIB-200 25.5; Qwen-0.5B 31.5/30.0/19.1; from-scratch 9B tokens 0-shot
findings.relevance: Direct evidence that 9B tokens from-scratch at 600M does NOT beat Qwen3-0.6B on knowledge QA — confirms the lab's continual-PT-from-Qwen3 default over from-scratch. SIB-200 result shows a Kazakh tokenizer alone buys large gains on lexical tasks.

findings.claim: Quality-filter + multi-epoch repetition beats single-pass diversity for a non-English language (German, from-scratch). From FineWeb-2-DE (496M docs), a DENSE-CORE filter = intersection of Coherence + Information-Value + Educational-Quality classifiers yielded only 5.1% (28B tokens); trained ~3.6 epochs to a 100B budget it beat the RANDOM single-pass 100B baseline by +4.89 avg (39.24 vs 34.35) at 350M, and +5.14 at 1B. Educational-Quality alone (33B, 3.0x) = 38.62.
findings.source: arXiv:2604.28075 (BOLDT / 'Repetition over Diversity'), Tables 1&3
findings.numbers: 350M @100B: DenseCore 28B unique x3.6ep = 39.24 avg vs Random 34.35 (+4.89); EduQuality 38.62; yields: EduQual 6.1%/33B, DenseCore 5.1%/28B of 496M docs
findings.relevance: transferable-untested (German is high-resource non-English, NOT Kazakh). Directly motivates building a Kazakh quality classifier + repeating a smaller high-quality core rather than dumping all ~9B raw tokens once (SozKZ's choice). Strongest 2026 evidence for the lab's data plan.

findings.claim: Multi-epoch repetition of a QUALITY-FILTERED core stays beneficial to ~7 epochs, extending the KB's 4-epoch rule for filtered data. BOLDT trained DENSE-CORE to a 200B budget = 7.2 epochs over the 28B subset and STILL gained +2.08 avg at 1B vs the 100B (3.6-epoch) run, with no observed saturation and no loss of instruction-tuning generalization. CRITICAL caveat: a core filtered by WEAK annotator/classifier models ('AA High') repeated 4.8x HURT — repetition only pays on genuinely high-quality data. Curriculum ordering (Phased 50/50 low->high, Sorted ascending edu-score) consistently UNDERPERFORMED a pure high-quality mix.
findings.source: arXiv:2604.28075 (BOLDT), sec 5.1-5.3, Tables 3&4
findings.numbers: 7.2 epochs on 28B core still +2.08 avg at 1B; Muennighoff 4-epoch extended; weak-filter core @4.8x degrades; Phased/Sorted curricula < pure DenseCore
findings.relevance: transferable-untested. Refines KB's '<=4 epochs ~= fresh tokens' rule: for a strongly-filtered Kazakh core the lab can safely repeat 4-7x, which is essential given only ~9-10B unique kk tokens. Also a design warning: do NOT do a low-quality->high-quality curriculum warmup, and use a STRONG LLM as the quality annotator.

findings.claim: Kazakh is ABSENT from FineWeb-C community educational-quality annotations (91 languages covered; kaz_Cyrl not among them). No FineWeb-Edu-style Kazakh quality classifier exists off the shelf. Cross-lingual transfer of the English FineWeb-Edu classifier onto translated text is documented not to work (picks up surface features that don't survive translation).
findings.source: danielvanstrien.xyz FineWeb-C analysis; huggingface.co/blog/davanstrien/fineweb-c; FineWeb-Edu classifier notes
findings.numbers: FineWeb-C: 91 languages, ~1,000 samples/lang, >50k annotations total; Kazakh = 0 annotations
findings.relevance: tested-on-Kazakh (absence confirmed). The lab must BOOTSTRAP its own kk quality classifier (e.g., annotate ~10-20k kk docs with a strong multilingual LLM, train a light regressor on mE5/XLM-R embeddings) — this is the single missing ingredient to apply the German/BOLDT recipe to Kazakh.

findings.claim: Machine-translated pretraining data works at scale but for languages NOT including Kazakh/Turkic. TransWebEdu = FineWeb-Edu translated into 9 langs (Arabic, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Welsh) = 1.7T tokens; a 1.3B model (Llama2 tokenizer) trained from scratch hit 45.08 avg vs Llama-3.2-1B 42.20 and Qwen2.5-1.5B 44.39, using ~10x less data. Russian portion = 157.4B tokens.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.13252 (Multilingual LM Pretraining using MT Data), Tables 2&8
findings.numbers: 9 langs, 1.7T tokens total (Russian 157.4B); 1.3B model avg 45.08 vs Llama3.2-1B 42.20 / Qwen2.5-1.5B 44.39; NO Kazakh/Turkic
findings.relevance: transferable-untested for Kazakh. Confirms MT-synthetic pretraining can match closed-data models — supports using English->Kazakh MT to inflate the ~9-10B pool. Russian is a covered high-resource language, relevant as kk's transfer/code-switch partner.

findings.claim: Filtered translationese for LOW-resource pretraining costs almost nothing vs clean data, if you filter with a tiny native LM. Translating 5B English tokens into Hindi/Gujarati/Marathi (IndicTrans2), then filtering with 28M/85M-param native LMs by perplexity (skip first 10 tok, score up to 1024 tok/doc), gave only -0.87% NLU and -2.35% NLG vs clean-data pretraining; adding ~10% clean native data (100-200M tokens) closed most of the remaining gap.
findings.source: arXiv:2403.13638 (Pretraining LMs Using Translationese, EMNLP 2024)
findings.numbers: 5B MT tokens; tiny-LM filter (28M/85M); filtered synthetic vs clean: NLU -0.87%, NLG -2.35%; +10% clean closes gap
findings.relevance: transferable-untested (Indic, not Turkic). Gives a concrete, cheap recipe for the synthetic portion: MT English->kk, filter with a small native-kk LM, and always append >=10% clean native kk to kill translationese. Bounds the synthetic risk that Sherkala took at 24% of its Kazakh mix.

findings.claim: Exact unique-token counts for the three primary Kazakh web sources (for de-duplication budgeting): CulturaX kk = 2,733,982 docs / 2,802,485,195 tokens (~2.80B, mT5 tokenizer, 0.04% of CulturaX's 6.3T). HPLT 2.0 deduplicated kaz_Cyrl = 1.409e9 (~1.41B whitespace tokens); HPLT2.0_cleaned kaz_Cyrl = 2.64M docs. FineWeb-2 kaz_Cyrl = 3.38M docs (rehydrated).
findings.source: huggingface.co/datasets/uonlp/CulturaX (kk row); arXiv:2503.10267 HPLT2.0 Table 5; HF HPLT/HPLT2.0_cleaned & HuggingFaceFW/fineweb-2 viewers
findings.numbers: CulturaX kk: 2,733,982 docs / 2,802,485,195 tok; HPLT2.0 dedup kk: 1.409B tok (cleaned 2.64M docs); FineWeb-2 kk: 3.38M docs
findings.relevance: tested-on-Kazakh (corpus artifacts). These three overlap heavily (all CommonCrawl-derived) — after cross-source fuzzy dedup the union is ~9-10B unique tokens, matching SozKZ's 9.0B post-dedup. Sets the hard unique-token budget the recipe must respect.

findings.claim: FineWeb-2 uses per-language dedup with 'rehydration': it keeps one doc per MinHash cluster but stores minhash_cluster_size, then UPSAMPLES documents by cluster size (per-language weights tuned to each language's cluster-filtering rate) rather than discarding duplicates — shown to improve downstream performance over both keep-all and drop-all-duplicates.
findings.source: arXiv:2506.20920 (FineWeb2) + HF fineweb-2 README (minhash_cluster_size field, rehydration code on GitHub)
findings.numbers: FineWeb-2: ~20TB/5B docs/1000+ langs; per-language MinHash dedup + cluster-size rehydration/upsampling
findings.relevance: transferable-untested at Kazakh scale. Concrete upgrade over SozKZ's MD5-exact dedup: adopt MinHash + cluster-size rehydration for the kk pool so the highest-cluster (most-duplicated, often canonical/clean) docs are upsampled — a principled alternative to blind Wikipedia 3x/multidomain 2x upsampling in the KB.

findings.claim: FineWeb2 (single multilingual pipeline) is reported to outperform CC-100, mC4, CulturaX and HPLT on downstream evals across languages while being substantially larger, and CulturaX<->FineWeb-2 share the most cross-corpus duplication (25.8B tokens overlap globally; C4<->CulturaX 25.5B).
findings.source: arXiv:2506.20920 (FineWeb2) / HF FineWeb2 card / MarkTechPost summary
findings.numbers: CulturaX∩FineWeb-2 = 25.8B tok overlap (global); FineWeb2 > CulturaX/HPLT/mC4 on downstream (per-language ablations)
findings.relevance: transferable-untested for kk specifically. Justifies making FineWeb-2 kk the QUALITY-primary web source and treating CulturaX kk as largely redundant with it (heavy overlap) — dedup CulturaX AGAINST FineWeb-2 rather than adding both naively.

findings.claim: Sherkala-8B (current kk SOTA, 41.4% KazMMLU) used a 45.3B continual-PT mix of kk:en:(ru+tr) = 3:1:3 (Kazakh 19.45B / English 19.45B / Russian+Turkish 6.4B), of which 24% of the Kazakh (~4.7B) was SYNTHETIC English-Wikipedia machine-translated to Kazakh; explicitly balanced to avoid English catastrophic forgetting.
findings.source: arXiv:2503.01493 (Sherkala) [via lab KB, verified]
findings.numbers: 45.3B: kk 19.45B (24% synthetic MT) / en 19.45B / ru+tr 6.4B; ratio 3:1:3
findings.relevance: tested-on-Kazakh. The only proven-at-SOTA Kazakh mixing ratio and synthetic fraction. But it targets an 8B model preserving English; a Kazakh-first 600M on limited compute should tilt far more toward kk (see recommendations). Caps synthetic at ~24% of kk as a safe SOTA-validated ceiling.

recommendations: UNIQUE POOL (~9-10B kk tokens): union CulturaX-kk (2.80B) + FineWeb-2-kk (3.38M docs, make it the quality-primary web source) + HPLT2.0-kk (1.41B) + MADLAD-400-kk + mC4-kk residual + Kazakh Wikipedia (~0.15B) + kz-transformers/multidomain-kazakh-dataset. Replace SozKZ's MD5-exact dedup with MinHash fuzzy dedup + FineWeb-2-style cluster-size REHYDRATION (upsample by duplicate-cluster size) instead of the KB's blind Wikipedia-3x/multidomain-2x. Expect ~9.0B unique post-dedup (matches SozKZ).

BUILD A KAZAKH QUALITY CLASSIFIER (missing ingredient — FineWeb-C has zero kk): annotate ~10-20k kk web docs for educational/informational value with a STRONG multilingual LLM (do NOT reuse the English FineWeb-Edu classifier on kk — cross-lingual transfer fails), train a light regressor on mE5-large/XLM-R embeddings. Keep the top ~30-40% as a 'kk-dense-core' (~3-4B tokens). BOLDT shows a WEAK-model filter repeated hurts, so annotator strength is non-negotiable.

MULTI-EPOCH PLAN: train the kk-dense-core for 4-7 epochs (BOLDT: 7.2 epochs still gained, no saturation), while the remaining lower-quality unique kk gets <=4 epochs (KB data-constrained rule). Do NOT use a low->high quality curriculum warmup — BOLDT's Phased/Sorted curricula underperformed a uniform high-quality mix; use a single uniform quality-weighted mixture.

MIXING for Kazakh-first CPT on Qwen3-0.6B-Base: target kk:ru:en ~= 70:15:15 (Kazakh-first; Russian included as the high-resource transfer + code-switch partner, English as replay against catastrophic forgetting). This tilts far more to kk than Sherkala's 43:14:43 because our model is 600M and Kazakh-first, not an 8B preserving English. Total training budget ~20-25B tokens = ~9-10B unique kk x ~2-2.5 effective epochs + ru/en replay drawn from CulturaX-ru / FineWeb-Edu.

SYNTHETIC DATA: cap MT-synthetic (English->kk) at <=25% of the Kazakh tokens (Sherkala SOTA-validated ceiling), filter it with a small native-kk LM by perplexity (2403.13638 recipe: 28-85M LM, skip first 10 tok, score <=1024 tok/doc), and always append >=10% clean NATIVE kk after synthetic to close the translationese gap (documented -0.87% NLU / -2.35% NLG cost, recoverable). Prefer NATURAL kk QA (WebFAQ-kaz ~12.5k, KazParC 372k) over MT where available.

COMPUTE FIT (free Kaggle T4x2, fp16, no bf16): T4 lacks bf16, so run QLoRA-CPT in fp16 with fp32 master weights / loss-scaling for stability (SozKZ and Sherkala both used bf16 which T4 can't) — verify no overflow on the SwiGLU/RMSNorm path. ~9-10B unique x 2-2.5 epochs is feasible in gradient-accumulated QLoRA increments; checkpoint per session (lab works in bursts).
open_questions: Exact FineWeb-2 kaz_Cyrl TOKEN count (only 3.38M doc count confirmed) — needed to finalize the unique-pool budget and the CulturaX-vs-FineWeb-2 overlap subtraction.

Cross-source duplication rate specifically among CulturaX-kk / FineWeb-2-kk / HPLT2.0-kk (all CommonCrawl-derived) — the ~9-10B union estimate assumes heavy overlap but the kk-specific MinHash overlap is unmeasured.

Does the German/BOLDT quality-filter + 7-epoch result hold when the UNIQUE pool is ~9B (Kazakh) rather than hundreds of billions (German)? BOLDT's own Limitations flag this is untested below German's corpus scale — the lab should run the ablation as a first experiment.

Whether MT-synthetic English->kk at 600M active params helps or triggers model collapse at the lab's low unique-data regime (Sherkala's 24% was at 8B with 45B tokens) — no sub-1B Kazakh evidence exists.
MADLAD-400-kk and mC4-kk exact deduplicated token counts after removing CulturaX/FineWeb-2 overlap — not found in primary sources this sweep.

findings.claim: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B is the strongest sub-1B multilingual embedder to beat and the natural v1 backbone: it is a decoder (Qwen3-0.6B) converted to an instruction-aware embedder that KEEPS causal attention and uses last-token [EOS] pooling (not bidirectional/mean). MRL output 32-1024 dims, 32k context, >100 languages.
findings.source: arXiv:2506.05176 (Qwen3 Embedding Technical Report); HF Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B card
findings.numbers: 0.6B params; emb dim 1024 (MRL 32-1024); 32k ctx; MTEB-Multilingual mean-task 64.33; MTEB-English v2 70.70; MTEB-Code 75.41; instruction format 'Instruct: {task}\nQuery:{q}'
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED (no Kazakh eval published). Since QymyzLM's v1 head sits on Qwen3-0.6B, this proves the exact backbone yields a top-tier 0.6B embedder with last-token+causal pooling — a drop-in template. Its 64.33 multilingual mean is the aspirational bar; but it is NOT evaluated on KazQAD/Kazakh.

findings.claim: Qwen3-Embedding's full training recipe is reproducible on free compute at the 0.6B scale: 3 stages — (1) contrastive pre-train on ~150M synthetic weak-supervision pairs generated by Qwen3-32B across retrieval/bitext/classification/STS; (2) supervised fine-tune on ~7M labeled pairs (MS MARCO, NQ, HotpotQA...) + ~12M high-quality synthetic pairs FILTERED by cosine>0.7; (3) checkpoint model-merging via spherical linear interpolation (slerp).
findings.source: arXiv:2506.05176 (html v1, Sec on training data)
findings.numbers: ~150M synthetic weak pairs (Qwen3-32B generator); ~7M labeled + ~12M synthetic supervised pairs; cosine-sim filter >0.7; merge = slerp of fine-tune checkpoints
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED. Confirms the model-soup/weight-averaging trick (slerp of checkpoints) that also underpins Less-is-More's 0.5/0.5 base-average — a cheap, compute-free gain for qymyz-embed. Synthetic-pair generation via a strong Kazakh LLM (Qwen3-32B/Sherkala) is the scalable route past the ~61k real Kazakh pair ceiling.

findings.claim: KaLM-Embedding-V2 is the current SOTA general embedder under 1B and the strongest published recipe on the SAME 0.5B-decoder class QymyzLM targets: Qwen2-0.5B (494M) with the causal mask REMOVED (bidirectional attention) + simple mean pooling + Matryoshka in both contrastive and KL losses. Trained ~470M pre-train pairs (InfoNCE, in-batch negatives) -> ~6M fine-tune pairs with hard negatives -> contrastive DISTILLATION from Qwen3-Embedding-8B teacher on the same 6M. Adds focal-style difficulty reweighting + online hard-negative mixing (Beta(2,2) pair-wise blend).
findings.source: arXiv:2506.20923 (KaLM-Embedding-V2, html v3); HF HIT-TMG/KaLM-embedding-multilingual-mini-instruct-v2
findings.numbers: 494M (Qwen2-0.5B), emb dim 896; MTEB avg 67.81 (v2), SOTA <1B; beats gte-Qwen2-1.5B(3x), e5-mistral-7b(14x); pre-train ~470M pairs, fine-tune ~6M, distill teacher Qwen3-Embedding-8B; Matryoshka keeps quality at 256-dim; focal weight w=(1-e^{s/τ}/Z)^γ
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED. Directly contradicts Qwen3-Embedding's causal+EOS choice: at 0.5B, KaLM WINS with bidirectional+mean pooling + teacher distillation. Distilling from Qwen3-Embedding-8B (or mE5-large) is a free-compute-friendly way to lift a 0.5B Kazakh head. This is the single best-matched recipe for v1 (QymyzLM head).

findings.claim: NV-Retriever's positive-aware hard-negative mining (TopK-PercPos) is the concrete recipe for evallab's pinned hard-negative protocol: mine top-k negatives with a teacher retriever, then DISCARD any candidate whose relevance score exceeds 95% of the positive's score (removes false negatives). This was the optimal setting and topped MTEB-Retrieval on release.
findings.source: arXiv:2407.15831 (NV-Retriever, Moreira et al. 2024)
findings.numbers: threshold = 95% of positive score (TopK-PercPos); NV-Retriever-v1 MTEB-Retrieval/BEIR 60.9, +0.65 over prior, #1 on 2024-07-07
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED on Kazakh. Fixes the exact protocol ambiguity the KB flags (mE5-large scores 0.449 vs 0.919 on KazQAD depending on candidate pool). Pin KazQAD hard-negatives via TopK-PercPos@95% with an mE5-large teacher over the 815k-passage corpus for a defensible, reproducible number.

findings.claim: gte-multilingual-base is a viable lighter alternative v0 base to mE5-large: 305M encoder (BERT+RoPE+GLU, XLM-R vocab), 8192 context, native MRL (128-768), and hybrid dense+sparse output, apache-2.0.
findings.source: arXiv:2407.19669 (mGTE); HF Alibaba-NLP/gte-multilingual-base
findings.numbers: 305M params; emb dim 768 (MRL 128-768); 8192 ctx; 70+ langs; apache-2.0; dense+sparse hybrid
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED on Kazakh. Half the size of mE5-large (560M) with long context + MRL + permissive license; a strong candidate if v0 needs a smaller/faster base than mE5, and the sparse head aids lexical Kazakh matching (agglutinative surface forms).

findings.claim: mmBERT is a 2025 modern multilingual ENCODER whose pretraining EXPLICITLY includes Kazakh — the only fresh encoder backbone in this sweep with confirmed kk coverage. Base 307M (110M non-emb), small 140M (42M non-emb), 256k vocab, 3T tokens, 1833 languages via annealed language learning. Not itself an embedding model (no contrastive head), but a from-scratch backbone option.
findings.source: arXiv:2509.06888 (mmBERT, JHU-CLSP); github.com/jhu-clsp/mmBERT
findings.numbers: base 307M/110M non-emb, small 140M/42M non-emb; vocab 256k; 3T tokens; 1833 langs incl. kaz; ctx 1024->8192; MTEB v2 multilingual 54.1 (base) vs XLM-R 52.4
findings.relevance: TESTED-ON-KAZAKH (pretraining coverage only; NO Kazakh embedding eval). Best modern encoder base if the lab wants an encoder path instead of decoder-conversion for v0; 256k vocab helps Kazakh fertility. Caveat: 54.1 MTEB-multilingual is well below mE5/KaLM as an out-of-box embedder — it needs a contrastive fine-tune to compete.

findings.claim: AfriE5 is the closest published analogue of qymyz-embed's task (adapt mE5 to low-resource languages) and gives a full transferable recipe: FINE-TUNE mE5-large-instruct via cross-lingual contrastive distillation from a BGE-reranker-v2-m3 cross-encoder teacher PLUS machine-translated NLI (MNLI/SNLI -> target langs via NLLB-200), quality-filtered by COMET>=0.75, ~60k pairs, 9 languages.
findings.source: arXiv:2510.23896 (AfriMTEB and AfriE5)
findings.numbers: ~60,066 pairs after COMET>=0.75 filter; 9 langs; AfriMTEB-Lite AfriE5 63.7 vs mE5-large-instruct 62.0 (+1.7); AfriMTEB-Full 62.4 vs 61.3 (+1.1)
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED on Kazakh (AfriMTEB has NO Turkic/Central-Asian langs). The +1.1/+1.7 gain from only ~60k MT+distilled pairs is a realistic ceiling estimate for a Kazakh mE5 fine-tune at the lab's ~61k real-pair scale — modest, matching the KB's kazembed +2.1% MRR datapoint. Distill-from-reranker + NLLB-MT of NLI is directly reusable for kk.

findings.claim: Turkic evidence (closest family to Kazakh) says beating mE5 is HARD even with a dedicated effort: TR-MTEB built 34.2M weakly-supervised Turkish pairs and trained Turkish-specific models with Matryoshka + two-stage NLI/STS fine-tuning, yet multilingual-E5 variants still LEAD the benchmark; Turkish-specific models are 'improving but not yet surpassing' mE5.
findings.source: TR-MTEB (ACL Findings EMNLP 2025, aclanthology 2025.findings-emnlp.471); TurkEmbed arXiv:2511.08376; TurkEmbed4Retrieval arXiv:2511.07595
findings.numbers: 34.2M weak Turkish pairs; Matryoshka + MNRL (All-NLI-TR) then CoSENT (STSB-TR); mE5 still #1 on TR-MTEB retrieval
findings.relevance: TESTED-ON-TURKIC. Sober calibration for the lab's 'beat mE5-large' target: a 34.2M-pair Turkish program did not dethrone mE5 on a same-family agglutinative language. Implies qymyz-embed must lean on (a) KazQAD-domain specialization and (b) distillation/model-soup, not raw pair volume, to win on KazQAD specifically.

findings.claim: Pooling/attention verdict at <=1B is unsettled and must be an ablation in the design spec: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B uses CAUSAL attention + last-token [EOS] pooling and reports it 'on par' with bidirectional+trainable pooling for most tasks; KaLM-V2 and LLM2Vec REMOVE the causal mask (bidirectional) + mean pooling and reach higher MTEB at the same 0.5B scale. Causal2Vec adds a lightweight bidirectional 'contextual token' prepended to a frozen-style decoder.
findings.source: arXiv:2506.05176 (Qwen3-Emb); arXiv:2506.20923 (KaLM-V2); arXiv:2507.23386 (Causal2Vec)
findings.numbers: Causal2Vec on Sheared-LLaMA-1.3B: MTEB avg 62.63 (+0.24 from contextual token); KaLM-V2 (bidir+mean) 67.81 vs Qwen3-Emb-0.6B (causal+EOS) 64.33 multilingual — different data, not iso-controlled
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED. For the QymyzLM head, the two live options are (A) causal+EOS+instruction (cheapest, reuses generation weights unchanged) vs (B) mask-removal+mean-pooling (higher ceiling per KaLM but needs re-adaptation). Not iso-controlled across papers, so the spec should A/B both on KazQAD.

findings.claim: Matryoshka Representation Learning is now standard in every sub-1B SOTA embedder (Qwen3-Emb 32-1024, KaLM-V2 to 256-dim, gte-multilingual 128-768) and costs ~nothing at train time — a nested-dim loss term applied to contrastive + KL losses, preserving quality at truncated dims.
findings.numbers: Qwen3-Emb MRL 32-1024; KaLM-V2 retains quality at 256-dim; gte-multilingual 128-768
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED. Free feature to ship in qymyz-embed v0/v1: enables 256-dim KazQAD retrieval indices (4x smaller than 1024) at minimal quality loss — matters for the on-device/modest-compute deployment story.

findings.claim: Slerp/checkpoint model-merging and base-weight-averaging is a cross-cutting free-compute win confirmed independently: Qwen3-Embedding merges fine-tune checkpoints via slerp; Less-is-More (KB) 0.5/0.5 averages the fine-tune with the base mE5. Both realize gains with zero extra training.
findings.source: arXiv:2506.05176 (slerp); arXiv:2603.22290 (Less-is-More, KB)
findings.numbers: Qwen3-Emb: slerp of multiple fine-tune checkpoints; Less-is-More: 0.5/0.5 weight-average with base mE5, ~10k pairs, lr 7e-5, batch 512, 5 epochs
findings.relevance: TRANSFERABLE-UNTESTED on Kazakh beyond Less-is-More itself. Extends the KB's Less-is-More entry: two independent SOTA recipes rely on weight-space merging, so qymyz-embed v0 should average multiple KazQAD fine-tunes (seed/data variants) via slerp, not just base-averaging.

findings.claim: The lab's mE5-large bar on KazQAD is protocol-bound, not a single number, and the only dedicated Kazakh embedder (kazembed-v5, mE5-base 278M) beat base mE5 by just +2.1% MRR from 61,255 pairs — consistent with AfriE5's +1.1/+1.7 and TR-MTEB's failure to surpass mE5.
findings.source: KB: HF Nurlykhan/kazembed-v5, shyngys879/kazakh-e5-rag-embedding cards; cross-ref AfriE5 arXiv:2510.23896
findings.numbers: mE5-large KazQAD: 0.4490 (HardTFIDF99) vs 0.9189 (KazQAD-100 local); kazembed-v5 MRR 0.835 (+2.1% over base); 61,255 pairs; full-corpus paper baseline MRR 0.382
findings.relevance: TESTED-ON-KAZAKH. Grounds the win-bar: small-pair fine-tunes yield only ~2% gains on same-family/low-resource langs. To beat mE5-large convincingly on KazQAD, qymyz-embed needs the FULL stack (TopK-PercPos hard negatives + teacher distillation + synthetic pair scaling + slerp), not just more real pairs.

recommendations: qymyz-embed v0 (mE5 base): keep mE5-large as base and stack the full free-compute recipe rather than relying on real-pair volume — (1) mine KazQAD hard negatives with NV-Retriever TopK-PercPos at 95%-of-positive threshold using mE5-large itself as teacher over the 815k-passage corpus; (2) scale training pairs past the ~61k real ceiling with Qwen3-32B/Sherkala-generated synthetic kk retrieval pairs filtered at cosine>0.7 (Qwen3-Emb recipe) plus NLLB-200 MT of English NLI filtered by COMET>=0.75 (AfriE5 recipe); (3) add contrastive distillation from a BGE-reranker-v2-m3 or Qwen3-Embedding-8B teacher; (4) ship Matryoshka (256/512/1024) and finish with slerp of multiple fine-tune checkpoints + 0.5/0.5 base-average (Less-is-More).

qymyz-embed v1 (Qwen3-0.6B / QymyzLM head): mirror KaLM-Embedding-V2 exactly since it is the same 0.5B-decoder class and current <1B SOTA — remove the causal mask (bidirectional attention) + mean pooling + Matryoshka-in-loss + focal reweighting + online hard-negative mixing + distillation from Qwen3-Embedding-8B. Run this as an A/B against the cheaper Qwen3-Embedding path (causal + last-token [EOS] + instruction-prefix, weights reused unchanged) on KazQAD; the pooling/attention verdict is NOT iso-controlled in the literature, so decide it empirically on KazQAD, not from cited averages.

Pin the KazQAD protocol in evallab before any headline number: report BOTH full-corpus retrieval (paper baseline MRR 0.382) AND a published TopK-PercPos@95% hard-negative pool; never quote a bare 'beat 0.909' since mE5-large ranges 0.449-0.919 on KazQAD by candidate-pool construction alone.

Set realistic win-bar expectations in the spec: Turkic (TR-MTEB, 34.2M pairs) and low-resource (AfriE5, ~60k pairs, +1.1/+1.7) evidence plus kazembed-v5 (+2.1% MRR) all show fine-tuning mE5 yields only single-digit-percent gains; budget for the full distillation+synthetic+merge stack and target KazQAD-domain specialization as the winning wedge, not generic multilingual mean.

Consider gte-multilingual-base (305M, apache-2.0, 8192 ctx, dense+sparse) as a lighter v0 alternative and mmBERT-base (307M, 256k vocab, Kazakh in pretraining) as the modern from-scratch encoder backbone if a decoder-conversion path is deprioritized; both need a contrastive fine-tune to reach mE5 territory (mmBERT out-of-box MTEB-multilingual 54.1).
open_questions: No published embedding model reports a KazQAD number under the lab's pinned full-corpus + TopK-PercPos protocol except mE5-large (0.449) and kazembed-v5 (0.835 on a non-comparable 100-candidate pool) — the true competitive gap for a fresh 0.6B Kazakh embedder is unmeasured.

Whether removing the causal mask (KaLM/LLM2Vec bidirectional) actually beats causal+EOS (Qwen3-Embedding) AT 0.6B on Kazakh retrieval specifically is untested; the two SOTA papers disagree and use non-iso data.
Does a shared QymyzLM backbone with a joint generative + embedding head (v1 vision) degrade either task versus separate models? No sub-1B multi-task-head Kazakh result exists.
Exact license of mmBERT weights was not confirmed in-source (repo present, license tag not stated in fetched content) — must verify before use as a backbone.

Whether Qwen3-32B / Sherkala-generated synthetic Kazakh retrieval pairs pass quality filtering at rates comparable to English (Qwen3-Emb kept cosine>0.7) is unknown for agglutinative kk with heavy kk/ru code-switching.

research.area: small-lm-training-recipes (QymyzLM design-panel input: optimizer, hyperparams for ~500M @ ~10B tokens, distillation, depth/width, fp16-on-T4 stability, CPT method choice)

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] DCLM 400M-1x is the closest published, fully-specified analog to a 500M/10B-token Kazakh run (412M params trained on 8.2B tokens, Chinchilla-1x). Verified from Table 10 of the paper PDF: 24 layers, 8 heads, d_model=1024, d_head=128, warmup 2000 steps, peak LR 3e-3, weight decay 0.033, z-loss 1e-4, global batch 512 sequences x 2048 tokens (~1.05M tokens/step, ~7.8k total steps), seq len 2048, GPT-NeoX 50k vocab. Architecture: pre-norm, LayerNorm without bias, qk-LayerNorm, SwiGLU, depth-scaled init, cross-document attention allowed (masking gave 'little impact'). HPs were tuned (following Gadre et al.) to optimize validation perplexity.
findings.source: arXiv:2406.11794 (DCLM), Table 10 + Appendix (read from PDF)
findings.numbers: 412M params / 8.2B tok; LR 3e-3; WD 0.033; z-loss 1e-4; warmup 2000 steps; batch 512x2048 = 1.05M tok; 24L/d1024/8H/dh128
findings.relevance: Drop-in tuned hyperparameter set at exactly the lab's from-scratch scale (500M @ 10B tok); removes the need for a muP sweep on free compute.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] MobileLLM-R1 (Meta, 2025) full open recipe at 140M/360M/950M: Adam beta=(0.9,0.95) eps 1e-8, WD 0.1 (pretraining only), peak LR 4.0e-3 with 2k-step warmup then linear decay to 0.1x peak; two pretraining phases of 2T tokens each at seq 2048 (global batch ~4M tok/step derived from 2T/500k steps; table lists per-device batch 16); mid-training 2x100B tokens at LR 3.6e-4 with knowledge distillation from Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct as teacher. All sizes use QK-norm and tied input/output embeddings, 128k vocab. Arch is NOT deep-narrow: 360M = 15 layers, d=1024, 16Q/4KV, FFN 4096 — the same Meta lineage that founded deep-narrow (MobileLLM 2024, 30-42L at 125M) shipped a shallow-wide 360M in 2025.
findings.source: arXiv:2509.24945 (MobileLLM-R1), Table 1 + training-details section (HTML)
findings.numbers: LR 4e-3 pretrain / 3.6e-4 mid-train; 4.2T total tokens; 360M: 15L/d1024/16Q/4KV/FFN4096; KD teacher Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct in mid-training
findings.relevance: Second independent LR anchor (3e-3..4e-3 at 360-500M with ~1-4M token batches); QK-norm+tied-embeddings consensus; weakens a blind deep-narrow default for QymyzLM — depth/width should be argued per-target, not by MobileLLM-2024 authority.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] MobileLLM-R1-950M matches/surpasses Qwen3-0.6B on reasoning with 11.7% of its tokens (4.2T vs 36T) but still loses on knowledge: base-model MMLU 47.4% (5-shot) vs Qwen3-0.6B 52.4%; MobileLLM-R1-360M-base: GSM8K 39.4% (8-shot), MATH500 13.4% (4-shot), MMLU 26.8% (5-shot) vs Qwen3-0.6B 60.9/29.8/52.4. Token-efficient recipes close reasoning gaps far faster than knowledge gaps.
findings.source: arXiv:2509.24945, Table 6 (base models)
findings.relevance: KazMMLU is a knowledge benchmark — a 500M model on ~10-40B effective Kazakh tokens cannot out-knowledge a 36T-token base by recipe alone; consistent with Engram-KB evidence that memory/lookup capacity, not recipe, is the knowledge lever. Beat-Qwen3 plan should lean on Kazakh-specific data + memory, not generic recipe gains.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] Muon (Moonlight paper) is validated down to 399M non-embedding params — inside the lab's scale: scaling-law fits give Muon loss 2.506*C^-0.052 vs AdamW 2.608*C^-0.054, i.e. ~52% of AdamW's training FLOPs to match performance. Required fixes to scale: (1) decoupled weight decay lambda=0.1 (W_t = W_{t-1} - eta*(O_t + lambda*W_{t-1})); (2) update-RMS matching: scale update by 0.2*sqrt(max(A,B)) to match AdamW's typical update RMS 0.2-0.4. Scaling-law runs: 399M-1.5B non-emb params, 8.92-38.91B tokens, LRs 9.5e-4..8.3e-4, batch 96-256 seqs @ 8K ctx. Muon stores ONE momentum buffer vs AdamW's two (half the optimizer memory). Caveat: paper runs Newton-Schulz iterations in bf16; fp16 NS on T4 (no bf16) is unvalidated anywhere.
findings.source: arXiv:2502.16982 (Muon is Scalable for LLM Training), Table 2 + Sec. 2 (HTML)
findings.numbers: ~52% FLOPs vs AdamW; smallest model 399M non-emb @ 8.92B tok; WD 0.1; RMS-match factor 0.2*sqrt(max(A,B)); 1 vs 2 momentum buffers
findings.relevance: At QymyzLM scale Muon halves optimizer VRAM (critical on 2x16GB T4) and roughly halves compute-to-loss — but the fp16-only constraint makes NS-iteration numerics the open risk; needs a cheap pilot (NS in fp32 costs little since it runs per-step on weight matrices).

findings.claim: [tested-on-Kazakh (as lab-measured baseline)] Qwen3-0.6B-Base, the CPT target, verified config from tech report: 28 layers, 16Q/8KV heads (GQA), tied embeddings, 32K context, vocab 151,669 byte-level BPE, QK-Norm in attention, SwiGLU+RoPE+pre-RMSNorm. Pretrained ~36T tokens in 3 stages (>30T general @ seq 4096; ~5T reasoning-heavy; hundreds of B long-context @ 32K). Lab already measured it at 32.8% KazMMLU 3-shot.
findings.source: arXiv:2505.09388 (Qwen3 Technical Report), Table 1 + Sec. 3; lab KB baseline table
findings.numbers: 28L, 16Q/8KV, vocab 151,669, tied emb, 36T tokens (30T+5T+~0.x T)
findings.relevance: (a) QK-norm is already inside Qwen3-0.6B — fp16 CPT on T4 inherits its attention-logit stability for free; (b) 151,669-token vocab with tied embeddings ≈ 155M embedding params at d=1024, ~26% of total — vocabulary surgery (Kazakh-focused vocab swap/prune) is the single biggest active-param lever for the ≤600M budget; (c) 36T-token base explains why the 32.8% KazMMLU bar is beatable mainly through Kazakh data, not general recipe.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] Qwen3's production strong-to-weak distillation pipeline covers 0.6B students (Qwen3-0.6B itself is a distilled student): phase 1 off-policy distillation on teacher outputs (/think + /no_think modes), phase 2 on-policy distillation — student generates sequences, then minimizes KL to teacher (Qwen3-32B or 235B-A22B) logits. Reported cost: ~1/10 the GPU hours of the full 4-stage post-training pipeline with better results. No per-pair benchmark table is published.
findings.source: arXiv:2505.09388, Sec. 4 (strong-to-weak distillation)
findings.numbers: students 0.6B-14B + 30B-A3B; teachers 32B/235B-A22B; 1/10 GPU hours vs 4-stage RL pipeline
findings.relevance: The best published sub-1B post-training recipe on free-compute budgets: after Kazakh CPT, on-policy logit-KL from any strong SAME-TOKENIZER teacher replaces RL. For QymyzLM the only same-tokenizer teachers are larger Qwen3 models (1.7B/4B fit T4 inference in 4-bit) — but their Kazakh quality is the bottleneck; untested for Kazakh.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] Distillation-vs-pure-next-token at pretraining, systematic study (Princeton, 2026): with LM/KD loss mixing coefficient alpha searched over {0.2,0.4,0.5,0.6,0.8,1.0}, even WEAK and SAME-SIZE teachers improve students — a 0.7B teacher trained on only 30B tokens still gives +1.3% downstream accuracy to a 1.7B student trained on 50B tokens. Stronger teachers saturate or REVERSE gains (8.0B teacher optimal alpha across 10/30/50/80/100/300B teacher tokens: 0.4,0.6,0.8,1.0,1.0,0.8 — non-monotone). Weaker teachers demand lower alpha (more ground-truth loss); pure KD (alpha=1.0) underperforms mixed loss for weak teachers. Findings replicate across student sizes 0.7B-8.0B (Table 3); gains show up in OOD/downstream more than in-domain ppl. Setup: Llama3-family, GQA 4:1, vocab 128,256, teachers 0.7B/1.7B/3.8B/8.0B x {10..300B} tokens.
findings.source: arXiv:2605.23857 (Strong Teacher Not Needed? On Distillation in LLM Pretraining), read from PDF
findings.numbers: alpha grid {0.2..1.0}; 0.7B@30B-tok teacher -> +1.3% downstream on 1.7B@50B student; 24 teacher configs; students 0.7B-8.0B
findings.relevance: Kazakh has NO strong teacher — this is the license to distill anyway: e.g., an early CPT checkpoint or same-size Kazakh model as teacher with low alpha (0.2-0.5) during from-scratch pretraining. Directly actionable and never tested on any low-resource language.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] OLMo 2 stability stack (adopted after diagnosing loss spikes): (1) QK-norm — RMSNorm on query/key projections before attention; (2) z-loss regularizer 1e-4 * log^2(Z) where Z is the softmax denominator over output logits; (3) switch nonparametric LayerNorm -> RMSNorm and reorder norms; (4) improved init. High LR (3.0e-3) caused instability/loss spikes in their setting, motivating the stack. Matches DCLM's independent choice of qk-LayerNorm + z-loss 1e-4 and Qwen3/MobileLLM-R1's QK-norm — 4-way convergence across 2024-2025 open recipes.
findings.source: arXiv:2501.00656 (2 OLMo 2 Furious), Sec. on training stability (via search-verified summary of the paper)
findings.numbers: z-loss coeff 1e-4; LR 3e-3 flagged unstable in OLMo2's config; QK-norm = RMSNorm on Q,K
findings.relevance: fp16-only T4 training amplifies exactly the two failure modes these fix (attention-logit growth, output-logit divergence: overflow at fp16's 65504 max). QK-norm + z-loss 1e-4 should be non-negotiable in any from-scratch QymyzLM config; z-loss additionally keeps logits in fp16-safe range.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] The Wortsman et al. small-scale-proxies paper — the cited foundation of DCLM's stability setup — shows the two dominant instabilities (attention-logit growth, output-logit divergence) reproduce in small models at high LR and are mitigated by qk-layernorm and z-loss respectively, flattening LR sensitivity across orders of magnitude of learning rate. Exact model sizes and sensitivity ranges not re-verified from the PDF this sweep.
findings.source: arXiv:2309.14322 (Small-scale proxies for large-scale Transformer training instabilities); cited as setup basis in arXiv:2406.11794 Appendix
findings.numbers: qk-layernorm -> attention-logit growth; z-loss -> output-logit divergence; 'orders of magnitude of learning rate variation' (abstract)
findings.relevance: Primary justification that stability interventions validated at small scale transfer to the lab's 500M fp16 regime; details flagged for one follow-up read before the design spec cites numbers.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] muP status 2025-2026: (a) CompleteP (arXiv:2505.01618, Cerebras, COLM/NeurIPS 2025) extends transfer to DEPTH and claims compute-efficiency gains for deep transformers over standard muP; (b) arXiv:2510.19093 argues weight decay, not muP, is the primary mechanism stabilizing update dynamics through most of training — muP's assumptions 'hold only briefly at the start' and its benefit is replaceable by modified warmup; (c) arXiv:2512.22382 (Dec 2025) unifies transfer across modules/width/depth/batch/duration. Net practice signal: for a SINGLE-SCALE 500M run, muP machinery buys little; tuned literature HPs (DCLM/SmolLM2/MobileLLM-R1 all in the 3e-3..4e-3 band with WD 0.033-0.1) + proper warmup are the 2025-2026 small-lab default.
findings.source: arXiv:2505.01618; arXiv:2510.19093; arXiv:2512.22382 (abstracts/HTML verified to exist and claims read; CompleteP efficiency percentages not pinned)
findings.numbers: LR consensus band at 350-500M: 3e-3 (DCLM 412M, SmolLM2-360M) to 4e-3 (MobileLLM-R1); WD 0.033 (DCLM) vs 0.1 (SmolLM2/MobileLLM-R1/Moonlight)
findings.relevance: Kills a whole tempting workstream: no muP sweep on free compute; adopt the converged HP band and spend the compute on data ablations instead.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] LoRA vs full fine-tuning for continued pretraining (Biderman et al.): in the CPT regime (20B unstructured tokens, code+math domains), standard low-rank LoRA substantially underperforms full finetuning; full FT learns weight perturbations of rank 10-100x typical LoRA configs. LoRA's advantage is forgetting mitigation (better retention of base-model capabilities than full FT even with regularization). Language acquisition (Kazakh) is a larger distribution shift than code/math — the underperformance risk is at least as bad.
findings.source: arXiv:2405.09673 (LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less), abstract-level verification this sweep
findings.numbers: CPT setting = 20B tokens; full-FT perturbation rank 10-100x LoRA rank; exact score gaps not extracted
findings.relevance: Direct challenge to the lab's QLoRA-CPT plan: for Kazakh CPT on Qwen3-0.6B, QLoRA will likely leave points on the table vs full FT. Counter-consideration: LoRA's forgetting resistance protects ru/en ability needed for kk/ru code-switching. Never tested on Kazakh — this is a cheap, high-value lab experiment (0.6B full-FT is feasible on T4x2, see recommendations).

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] SmolLM3-3B (HF, 2025) recipe deltas vs SmolLM2 relevant downscale evidence: AdamW (0.9,0.95), WD 0.1, grad clip 1.0, WSD schedule with 2000 warmup steps and linear decay to 0 over final 10%, global batch 2.36M tokens @ seq 4096, 11.2T tokens, LR 2e-4 (3B-scale — NOT transferable to 500M, where SmolLM2 used 3e-3). Confirms the pattern: peak LR falls ~10-15x from 360M to 3B; warmup ~2000 steps is scale-invariant across DCLM/MobileLLM-R1/SmolLM3.
findings.source: https://huggingface.co/blog/smollm3 (search-verified); SmolLM2 arXiv:2502.02737 (KB)
findings.numbers: 2e-4 @ 3B vs 3e-3 @ 360M; warmup 2000 steps in 4/4 modern recipes; batch 2.36M tok
findings.relevance: Locks warmup=2000 steps and the LR-vs-scale curve for the design spec; warns against copying any 1B+ LR downward.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] Compute feasibility re-derivation for from-scratch on Kaggle T4x2: 6*N*D = 6 * 5e8 * 1e10 = 3e19 FLOPs. T4 fp16 peak 65 TFLOPS; at an optimistic 25% MFU, 2 GPUs deliver ~3.25e13 FLOP/s -> ~9.2e5 s ~ 256 wall-clock hours ~ 8.5+ weeks of Kaggle's ~30 GPU-h/week quota for ONE epoch-equivalent pass — before checkpoint/restart overhead of 12h session caps, and T4 realistic MFU for small models is usually 10-20%, i.e. 400-650 hours. Combined with the KB's data-constrained law (<=4 epochs useful: 9-10B corpus -> <=40B useful tokens), a full Chinchilla-style from-scratch run is a multi-month commitment; QLoRA/full CPT on Qwen3-0.6B at 1-3B Kazakh tokens is 1-2 orders of magnitude cheaper.
findings.source: Re-derived from 6ND formula + NVIDIA T4 spec (65 TFLOPS fp16) + Kaggle quota (30 GPU-h/week, 12h sessions); KB arXiv:2305.16264
findings.numbers: 3e19 FLOPs; 256-650 T4x2 wall-hours depending on MFU 10-25%; Kaggle ~30 h/week
findings.relevance: Hard constraint for the design panel: 'from-scratch later' requires either token-budget cuts (5B tokens halves it), Muon's ~2x FLOP efficiency, or paid/pooled compute; CPT-now is the only schedule-feasible path.

findings.claim: [transferable-untested] fp16-only (pre-Ampere) training practice, synthesized from the verified stability stack (no single paper tests T4 specifically): dynamic loss scaling with fp32 master weights (standard AMP GradScaler), z-loss 1e-4 (bounds output logits well inside fp16 max 65504), QK-norm (bounds attention logits), RMSNorm and softmax computed in fp32, grad clip 1.0 (SmolLM3/OLMo2). AdamW eps 1e-8 is fine with fp32 optimizer states; never keep optimizer states in fp16. Flash-attention on T4 (SM75) is supported only by FlashAttention-1-era/xformers kernels, not FA2 — memory-efficient attention via PyTorch SDPA (efficient backend) is available.
findings.source: Synthesis of arXiv:2501.00656, 2406.11794, 2309.14322 + NVIDIA AMP documentation; SM75 FA2 exclusion is from flash-attention repo requirements (Ampere+)
findings.numbers: z-loss 1e-4; grad clip 1.0; fp16 max 65504; FA2 requires SM80+, T4=SM75
findings.relevance: The exact fp16 checklist the design spec needs; every element is individually sourced but the combined recipe on T4 for Kazakh is untested — pilot on the first 100M-token CPT run.

recommendations: Recommended from-scratch hyperparameter table for ~500M @ ~10B Kazakh tokens on T4x2 (all [transferable-untested]; anchor = DCLM 400M-1x, the tuned run closest to this exact scale): arch 24L x d1024 x 8-16H (dh 64-128), GQA 4:1, SwiGLU, tied embeddings, vocab 48-64k Kazakh-centric BPE; optimizer AdamW beta=(0.9,0.95) eps 1e-8, WD 0.033-0.1; peak LR 3e-3, warmup 2000 steps, WSD or cosine with decay to <=0.1x peak (anneal on cleanest data in final 10-20% per SmolLM2); global batch ~1M tokens (512x2048 via gradient accumulation; if forced to ~0.25M, drop LR to ~1.5e-3); seq 2048; stability: QK-norm + z-loss 1e-4 + RMSNorm-no-bias + depth-scaled init + grad clip 1.0 + fp32 master weights with dynamic loss scaling; data: <=4 epochs of the 9-10B corpus (KB law).

CPT-now path: before committing to QLoRA, run the cheap head-to-head the literature demands (arXiv:2405.09673): full-parameter fp16 CPT of Qwen3-0.6B is VRAM-feasible on T4x2 (weights 1.2GB fp16 + fp32 master 2.4GB + AdamW states 4.8GB ≈ 8.4GB, splittable via ZeRO-2/FSDP across 2x16GB with activation checkpointing) — compare vs QLoRA r=64-256 on identical 100-300M Kazakh tokens, scoring both KazMMLU delta AND ru/en retention (LoRA's forgetting advantage matters for kk/ru code-switching).

Distillation plan: (1) post-CPT, adopt Qwen3's off-policy->on-policy logit-KL pipeline with a same-tokenizer teacher (Qwen3-1.7B/4B, 4-bit on T4) — but FIRST measure the teacher's own Kazakh quality; a bad teacher with high alpha is worse than none. (2) If from-scratch happens, mix KD into pretraining with LOW alpha (0.2-0.5) from whatever same-level Kazakh-capable model exists (e.g., the lab's own CPT'd Qwen3-0.6B) per arXiv:2605.23857 — weak/same-level teachers verifiably help; do not chase a 'strong' multilingual teacher.

Optimizer decision: default AdamW (all HPs de-risked); schedule one pilot of Muon with WD 0.1 + 0.2*sqrt(max(A,B)) RMS matching and Newton-Schulz in fp32 (bf16-NS is the published setting; fp16-NS unvalidated) — if stable, it roughly halves both compute-to-loss and optimizer VRAM, the two binding T4 constraints.

Skip muP entirely for single-scale work; spend saved compute on data-mixture ablations (DCLM's core result: curation rank-correlates r=0.838 from 400M-1x to 7B-1x, so 400M-scale Kazakh data ablations are trustworthy signals for any later scale-up).

Vocabulary surgery on Qwen3-0.6B is the top active-param lever: 151,669-vocab tied embedding ≈ 155M params (~26% of model) at d=1024; pruning to a Kazakh+ru+en-focused 60-80k vocab frees 70-95M active params for transformer blocks or an Engram-style memory while directly attacking fertility (target <2.0 tok/word).

Set expectations per MobileLLM-R1 evidence: recipe+data efficiency closes reasoning gaps at ~10% token budgets, but knowledge (MMLU-type, i.e., KazMMLU) lags — pair the training recipe with a knowledge-capacity mechanism (Engram memory, KB-verified) rather than expecting recipe alone to add +3-4pp KazMMLU.
open_questions: Does fp16 (not bf16) Newton-Schulz iteration in Muon stay numerically stable at 500M scale on T4? No published evidence; needs a 100M-token pilot with fp32-NS fallback.

Exact quantitative LoRA-vs-full gap in the CPT setting of arXiv:2405.09673 (abstract-level only this sweep) — read Tables before the design panel cites it; also whether any 2025-2026 work tested (Q)LoRA-CPT specifically for LANGUAGE acquisition rather than code/math domains.

CompleteP's exact compute-efficiency numbers for deep-narrow models (arXiv:2505.01618) — relevant only if the panel picks a >32-layer deep-narrow config, where depth-wise transfer/stability claims would matter.
Wortsman et al. (2309.14322) exact model sizes and LR-sensitivity ranges — one PDF read to firm up the two uncertain stability findings.

What batch size is optimal at only ~7-10k total steps (10B tokens / 1M batch)? All anchor recipes trained 100k+ steps; whether 2000-step warmup + 1M-token batch is too coarse for a 10B-token run is untested — consider 0.5M batch / LR 2e-3 as a hedge.

Is there ANY published Turkic-language from-scratch or CPT run with disclosed hyperparameters besides SozKZ (KB) to serve as a tested-on-Turkic anchor? This sweep found none in the recipe literature — worth a targeted kk/tr-language sweep.

conflicts: LR SCHEDULE (unresolved across the 3 strongest CPT recipes): NVIDIA 'Reuse Don't Retrain' — 'start at η_min of pretraining (4.5e-5), NO warmup ... explicitly warns re-warming a heavily-trained base can hurt'; Ibrahim 2403.08763 — 're-warm to high LR then re-decay (+replay) ... not re-warming slows adaptation'; Sailor — 'constant 1e-4'; EstLLM — 'trapezoidal WSD'. Qwen3-0.6B is a heavily-overtrained base, so NVIDIA's caution applies directly — the continual-pt researcher states 'do not average' these.

LoRA vs FULL FINETUNE in CPT (opposite conclusions by data regime): LLiMba (11.5M tokens) — 'rsLoRA r=256 reached 28.5 BLEU vs full fine-tuning 21.0' (LoRA wins); vs LoRA-Learns-Less (20B tokens) — 'LoRA r=256 GSM8K 0.203 vs full FT 0.293' and BLOOM+1 — 'full CPT best at 560M, adapters win only above ~3B' (full wins). The lab's ~10B-token regime sits on the full-FT side.

EMBEDDING POOLING at 0.5-0.6B (not iso-controlled): KaLM-V2 (bidirectional + mean pooling) MTEB 67.81 vs Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (causal + last-token EOS) 64.33 — 'different data, not iso-controlled'; Qwen3-Embedding claims causal+EOS is 'on par with bidirectional+trainable pooling for most tasks'.

DOES MEMORY HELP DENSE SUB-1B (regime-dependent): POSITIVE — TN-gram 9L 'raw BPB 1.251 -> Engram 1.209 -> TN-gram 1.208' and MolGram 'MolGram-GPT 6.7M = 42.09% vs MolGPT 25.5M = 41.68%' (both at vocab 100-1,024); NEGATIVE — Memory Grafting 'vanilla-Engram 45.03 vs MoE 45.62' (production vocab, MoE). Positives only exist in high-fertility/sub-lexical-token regimes.

HASH COLLISIONS as the sub-1B killer (direct contradiction): Engram-Nine — 'Hash-500K val loss 4.4809 vs collision-free Nine-100/400K 4.4799 — delta 0.001, not significant; collisions act as implicit regularization'; directly counters Memory Grafting's narrative (KB) that hash collisions are the sub-1B killer.
KAZAKH 8B KazMMLU DATAPOINTS: ISSAI KazLLM-1.0-8B '37.0' vs Sherkala-Chat-8B '41.4'; and within Sherkala 'base 51.6 vs chat 41.4' (instruct-tuning costs ~-10pp).

QWEN3-0.6B VOCAB COUNT (verbatim discrepancy): tokenizer area 'Vocab is 151,643/151,936'; small-lm and continual-pt areas 'vocab 151,669'; attention area reconciles as '151936 = padded embedding rows, 151,669 = tokenizer token count' — the 151,643 figure is unreconciled.

gapFills.area: Hardware gate: do FLA (Gated DeltaNet/KDA), Mamba2, and Muon Newton-Schulz kernels run on SM75 (Kaggle T4 class, fp16-only), and at what throughput

findings.claim: GATE OPEN: all three kernel families RUN on SM75 in fp16 with finite outputs and gradients. We executed the actual ~30-min smoke test on an RTX 2070 laptop GPU (compute capability (7,5) — identical SM75 codegen target as Kaggle T4, same 64KB shared-memory/SM limit, no bf16 tensor cores) with torch 2.11.0+cu130, triton 3.6.0, flash-linear-attention (fla) 0.5.1: GatedDeltaNet PASS, KimiDeltaAttention (KDA) PASS, fla's Triton Mamba2 PASS, all fwd+bwd, torch.isfinite(out/grad)=True. Flag: transferable-untested (language-agnostic hardware gate; never before run for this lab).
findings.source: Empirical, this session: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-altairzhambyl-projects-SLMs-basic/98053e10-7c62-465c-acd3-b6c763138a63/scratchpad/smoke2.py on local RTX 2070 (SM75); fla 0.5.1 from PyPI (github.com/fla-org/flash-linear-attention)
findings.numbers: fp16 fwd+bwd, B=2, T=1024, d=768, 6 heads: KDA 14.2 ms (144,270 tok/s/layer); GatedDeltaNet 144.3 ms (14,196 tok/s/layer); fla-Mamba2 (12 heads, head_dim 128) 245.6 ms (8,338 tok/s/layer); torch SDPA baseline 5.2 ms (397,144 tok/s/layer)
findings.relevance: Un-blocks the linear/SSM hybrid branch (GDN-H1-style, Falcon-H1-style) and Muon for the design panel: nothing hard-fails on Kaggle T4-class hardware. QLoRA-CPT v1 and from-scratch v2 menus can both legally include these components.

findings.claim: THROUGHPUT INVERSION at training-relevant context lengths: on SM75 the classic linear-attention speed motivation is inverted. torch SDPA (softmax attention, fp16) is FASTER per layer than every linear kernel up to at least T=8192; KDA only breaks even around T~12-16K (extrapolated from linear-vs-quadratic trend). For a 10B-token CPT run at ctx 1024-4096, a KDA layer costs 2.7-4.8x an SDPA layer; fla-0.5.1 GatedDeltaNet and Mamba2 layers cost 28-47x SDPA (they appear to hit fallback/small-block Triton configs under the 64KB shared-memory limit). If a hybrid is specced for v2, KDA is currently the only fla linear kernel with acceptable SM75 throughput. Flag: transferable-untested.
findings.source: Empirical, this session: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-altairzhambyl-projects-SLMs-basic/98053e10-7c62-465c-acd3-b6c763138a63/scratchpad/crossover.py (fp16, B=1, d=768)
findings.numbers: fwd+bwd per layer — T=2048: KDA 13.5 ms vs SDPA 4.3 ms (3.1x); T=4096: 26.0 vs 12.6 ms (2.1x); T=8192: 51.3 vs 42.1 ms (1.2x); KDA throughput flat ~151-160K tok/s/layer (linear scaling confirmed), SDPA decays 480K->194K tok/s/layer
findings.relevance: The panel should not adopt a hybrid for THROUGHPUT on T4x2 — only for quality (+4.2pp GDN-H1-class) or KV-cache reasons; and the 10B-token compute budget must price linear layers at 2-5x attention cost at our context lengths.

findings.claim: Muon IS usable on T4, but the official implementation contains a 6.6x SM75 performance trap: KellerJordan/Muon's zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 hard-casts to bfloat16 ('X = G.bfloat16()', 5 iterations, coefficients a,b,c = 3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315), and bf16 matmul on SM75 is software-emulated. NS5 in fp16 is numerically equivalent (input is norm-normalized to ~[0,1] first, so fp16 range is safe) and runs on tensor cores. One-line patch (.bfloat16() -> .half()) makes Muon fast on T4. Optimizer state is a single momentum buffer per param (state['momentum_buffer'] = torch.zeros_like(p)) — the ~50% optimizer-VRAM saving vs AdamW's two moments is structurally confirmed. Flag: transferable-untested (never run on a Kazakh model).
findings.source: Empirical: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-altairzhambyl-projects-SLMs-basic/98053e10-7c62-465c-acd3-b6c763138a63/scratchpad/muon_ns.py + code read of raw.githubusercontent.com/KellerJordan/Muon/master/muon.py
findings.numbers: NS5 on a 2048x5632 matrix (600M-class FFN weight), SM75: bf16 189.6 ms, fp32 120.4 ms, fp16 28.9 ms per matrix; orthogonalization quality identical — singular values of output in [0.673,1.137] (bf16), [0.682,1.135] (fp16), [0.682,1.134] (fp32), all finite
findings.relevance: Muon's ~2x data-efficiency claim (Moonlight, arXiv 2502.02982) is reachable on free T4 compute for the from-scratch v2 track, but ONLY with the fp16 patch; unpatched Muon would burn ~6.6x optimizer wall-clock in NS.

findings.claim: bf16 on SM75 is a silent trap across the stack: torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported() returns True on SM75 (torch 2.11), and bf16 Triton kernels compile and run — but without tensor cores. Measured bf16 GEMM is 7.3x slower than fp16 and even 1.7x slower than fp32. All fla kernels pass in bf16 but at 1.2-1.6x their fp16 time. Every training config for Kaggle T4 must pin fp16 + GradScaler and must not trust the bf16 capability flag. Flag: transferable-untested.
findings.source: Empirical: muon_ns.py and smoke2.py this session (torch 2.11.0+cu130, SM75)
findings.numbers: 4096^3 matmul: fp16 20.93 TFLOPS (tensor cores), bf16 2.88 TFLOPS, fp32 4.83 TFLOPS; KDA bf16 22.8 ms vs fp16 14.2 ms (1.6x); GDN bf16 175.0 vs 144.3 ms (1.2x); Mamba2 bf16 253.8 vs 245.6 ms
findings.relevance: Design-panel configs copied from 2025-26 papers (all bf16-native) will run but silently lose most tensor-core throughput on T4; loss-scaling (GradScaler) requirements of fp16 must be part of the training recipe, including for Engram gating and QLoRA-CPT.

findings.claim: First-call Triton compile/autotune cost on SM75 is large and per-session on Kaggle: KDA's first fwd+bwd took 439 s (fp16) / 523 s (bf16); GDN bf16 388 s; fla-Mamba2 34-42 s. findings.claim: Fraction-of-A100 context for all measured numbers: T4 peak is ~21% of one A100 on both axes, and Kaggle gives two of them. NVIDIA official specs: T4 = 65 TFLOPS FP16 mixed-precision, 8.1 TFLOPS FP32, 16 GB GDDR6 at '320+ GB/s', 70 W; A100-40GB = 312 TFLOPS BF16/FP16 tensor, 1555 GB/s. So T4/A100 = 20.8% peak fp16 compute, ~20.6% bandwidth; T4x2 aggregate ~41.7% of one A100 (data-parallel, if both GPUs used). Proxy caveat: our absolute ms were measured on an 80W RTX 2070 laptop (SM75, ~45 fp16 tensor TFLOPS peak, 448 GB/s); actual T4 should be within roughly ±40% on absolute times (faster on compute-bound, slower on bandwidth-bound kernels) with identical PASS/FAIL and dtype behavior.

recommendations: Un-gate the hybrid branch for the design panel, but re-price it: KDA (fla 0.5.1, fp16, mode='chunk') is the ONLY linear kernel with acceptable SM75 throughput today (2.1-3.1x SDPA cost at ctx 2-4K); do not spec GDN- or Mamba2-heavy stacks on current fla kernels without first resolving their 28-47x SM75 slowdown (likely autotune/shared-memory config; file an fla-org issue with our numbers).
Keep v1 (QLoRA-CPT on Qwen3-0.6B) on pure softmax SDPA fp16 — measured fastest path on SM75, no FA2 needed; optionally evaluate the flash-attention-turing port after one verification pass.

Adopt Muon for any from-scratch v2 run with a one-line patch: change zeropower_via_newtonschulz5's X = G.bfloat16() to .half() (measured 6.6x NS speedup on SM75, numerically equivalent: sv range 0.682-1.135 vs 0.673-1.137).
